title: Exact curve restriction, classical realization and local spectra
statement: Fix $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k_0$, $\Qlb=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and $\iota:\Qlb\simeq\mathbf C$ [def-weil-punctual-weights]. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, $m\ge1$, $k_m=\mathbf F_{q^m}\subset k$, and let $h_m:C_m\hookrightarrow X_{0,m}=X_0\times_{k_0}k_m$ be a closed immersion with $C_m$ finite type over $k_m$ [def-weil-closed-immersion; def-weil-finite-type-morphism; def-pc-base-change]. For the classical lisse sheaves of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves], equipped with Weil isomorphisms [def-wf-fundamental-representation], let $0=\mathcal G_0\subset\cdots\subset\mathcal G_r=\mathcal G$ be a finite filtration by lisse Weil subsheaves with lisse quotients $\mathcal S_j$. Realize them in the common-stage Weil heart [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex; def-weil-constructible-heart; def-real-common-stage-lisse]. Define $R_m$ to be constant restriction with the iterated $m$th Weil map, followed by $h_m^*$ [def-dl-a1-constant-extension-data; def-zl-constant-extension-restriction-local-data; def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Then $R_m$ is exact on these filtrations: $0=R_m\mathcal G_0\subset\cdots\subset R_m\mathcal G_r=R_m\mathcal G$ has quotients canonically $R_m\mathcal S_j$, all classically lisse. Its geometric sheaves are ordinary pullbacks to $(C_m)_k$. The classical and common-stage identifications commute with these maps, their composites, the Weil maps and local geometric Frobenius, including iterated point transports. For each closed $z\in C_m$, its image $x\in X_0$ is closed, $f=[\kappa(z):\kappa(x)]\ge1$, and the canonical stalk identification conjugates $F_{z,R_mH}$ to $F_{x,H}^f$ for each filtration term or quotient $H$. In particular $q_z=q_x^f$ and $\operatorname{Eig}(F_{z,R_mH})=\{\alpha^f:\alpha\in\operatorname{Eig}(F_{x,H})\}$ as multisets with algebraic multiplicities [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace; def-wf-iota-real]. If $\mathcal G$ is $\iota$-real, so is $R_m\mathcal G$, including when distinct eigenvalues acquire equal powers. The assertion permits $r=0$ and imposes no semisimplicity or diagonalizability hypothesis.

proof.text: Install the inherited separatedness and prime-unit instances. Apply lem-zl-curve-classical-pullback-exists to the supplied R and realizations, obtaining c and lissity of all restricted classical carriers.

Apply lem-zl-curve-classical-filtration-pullback to F to obtain geometric zero and exactness proof fields. Construct the curve filtration directly with terms, quotients and arrows defined by c.classical. Apply lem-zl-classical-weil-filtration-heart-transport to F on X and to this filtration on C. Choose the curve top isomorphism as the inverse realization component followed by restriction of the given e.

Map the defining classical term equalities to isomorphisms under the curve realization, and compose them with the realization comparison. Generic functoriality and naturality give both arrow squares. Cancel the final isomorphism to prove the restricted composite is zero; construct the isomorphism of short complexes and transfer short exactness by ShortComplex.shortExact_iff_of_iso. Transfer the zero initial term by IsZero.of_iso, first transporting the two finite zero indices explicitly along their equality so that realization functors need not unfold to identify them. Mapping the reflexive classical top equality gives heterogeneous equality with the prescribed inverse realization component followed by restriction of e.

Apply lem-zl-curve-restriction-local-powers to every realized classical term or quotient, obtaining its local conclusions, and to G itself, obtaining preservation of reality. Together with the lissity from the first step and both transport records, these are all conjuncts of the unchanged assertion. Empty indices introduce no extra condition.

B7 Lean assembly via normalized classical pullback, classical filtration pullback and local residue powers; exactness is transported by an explicit short-complex isomorphism.

I read each cited statement and found no cycle (BFS over 17,885 nodes). Step 1: the permanence nodes (base change, closed immersion finite, finite after separated finite-type) supply the Noetherian separated finite-type hypotheses. Step 2: filtration-heart-transport gives the exact heart sequences at a common finite stage. Step 3: constant-extension (a) and immersion part 1 (valid over any F_q, hence over k_m) are both exact, so R_m is exact. Steps 4-5: diagram-realization, completed-system and rational-realization pullback comparisons (natural, with identity and composition laws) show the terms are classically lisse with ordinary-pullback geometric sheaves. The iterate-comparison lemma covers the point transports and their regrouping over F_{q^m}. Step 6: the immersion lemma gives κ(y)≅κ(z) and b. Constant-extension (a) gives F_x^e. That lemma only says 'conjugate', but the carrier is unchanged, so the stalk identification is canonical. This gives f=e and c=ab. Steps 7-8: the power-spectrum lemma (algebraic multiplicities, no semisimplicity) and def-wf-iota-real give the spectrum and reality, including collisions. Step 9 (r=0, empty C_m) is elementary. Source checked: Weil II §1.1 p.146 says the Frobenius at z is the n-th power of the Frobenius at y when [k(z):k(y)]=n. Edge cases tested: q=2,m=2,d=2 gives f=1, not m; i and -i squared collide at -1 with multiplicity 2; Jordan block; rank zero; empty or disconnected C_m. No SGA is cited.
